tools.name: workspace_metadata
tools.description:
Use this to discover workspace entities and canonical IDs (viewer, teams, workflow states, labels, projects, favorites). Use this FIRST whenever you don't know ids. Inputs: include? (profile|teams|workflow_states|labels|projects|favorites), teamIds?, project_limit?, label_limit?.
Returns: viewer, teams[] (with estimation settings and cyclesEnabled), workflowStatesByTeam, labelsByTeam, projects[], favorites?. Next: Use teamId/projectId to filter 'list_issues'; use workflowStatesByTeam[teamId][].id as stateId for 'update_issues'; use labelsByTeam ids for label operations. If a team has cyclesEnabled=false, avoid cycle-related tools.

include.description: What to include. Defaults to ['profile','teams','workflow_states','labels','projects']. 'profile' returns viewer (id, name, email, timezone). 'teams' returns team list with cyclesEnabled flag. 'workflow_states' returns workflowStatesByTeam[teamId] with state id/name/type. 'labels' returns labelsByTeam[teamId]. 'projects' returns project list. 'favorites' returns user favorites.

teamIds.description: Filter to specific team UUIDs. If omitted, fetches all teams.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description:
List issues with filtering. Inputs: teamId?, projectId?, filter?, q?, keywords?, matchMode?, includeArchived?, orderBy?(updatedAt|createdAt), detail?(minimal|standard|full), limit?, cursor?, assignedToMe?.

⚠️ orderBy only supports updatedAt or createdAt. DO NOT use orderBy:"priority" - use filter instead!

KEYWORD SEARCH (q/keywords):
- q: Extract 2-4 significant keywords from user intent. Avoid short/common words.
- matchMode: 'all' (default, precise) requires ALL tokens; 'any' (broad) requires at least ONE.
- Example: user says "find cursor workshop task" → q: "cursor workshop"

FILTERING:
- High priority: filter: { priority: { lte: 2 } } (1=Urgent, 2=High, 3=Medium, 4=Low)
- Active issues: filter: { state: { type: { neq: 'completed' } } }
- In progress: filter: { state: { type: { eq: 'started' } } }
- My issues: assignedToMe: true

DETAIL LEVELS: minimal (id,title,state), standard (default, +priority,assignee,project), full (+labels,description).

Returns: { items[], pagination, meta }.

filter.description: GraphQL-style IssueFilter. Structure: { field: { comparator: value } }. Comparators: eq, neq, lt, lte, gt, gte, in, nin, containsIgnoreCase, startsWith, endsWith. Examples: { state: { type: { eq: 'started' } } } for in-progress, { state: { type: { neq: 'completed' } } } for open issues, { assignee: { email: { eqIgnoreCase: 'x@y.com' } } }, { labels: { name: { in: ['Bug', 'Urgent'] } } }, { title: { containsIgnoreCase: 'search' } }.

orderBy.description: Sort order. Default: 'updatedAt'. Note: To prioritize high-priority issues, use filter: { priority: { lte: 2 } } instead.

detail.description: Detail level: 'minimal' (id, title, state), 'standard' (+ priority, assignee, project, due), 'full' (+ labels, description). Default: 'standard'.

q.description: Free-text search query. Splits into tokens by whitespace, matches title case-insensitively. Use 2-4 significant keywords extracted from user intent. Avoid short/common words. Example: user says 'find my task about the cursor workshop' → q: 'cursor workshop'

keywords.description: Explicit keywords for title search. Uses matchMode logic (default: all must match).

matchMode.description: How keyword tokens are matched: 'all' requires ALL tokens present in title (precise, default), 'any' requires at least ONE token (broad, use for exploratory searches).

assignedToMe.description: If true, only show issues assigned to the current viewer. Shortcut for filter.assignee.id.eq with viewer ID.

tools.name: get_issues
tools.description:
Fetch detailed issues in batch by ids (UUIDs or short ids like ENG-123). Inputs: { ids: string[] }.
Returns: { results: Array<{ index, ok, id?, identifier?, issue? }>, summary }. Each issue includes assignee, state, project, labels, attachments, and branchName when available. Next: Call 'update_issues' to modify fields or 'list_issues' to discover more.

ids.description: Issue IDs to fetch. Accepts UUIDs or short identifiers like ENG-123.

tools.name: create_issues
tools.description:
Create multiple issues in one call. Inputs: { items: Array<{ teamId: string; title: string; description?; stateId?; stateName?; stateType?; labelIds?; labelNames?; assigneeId?; assigneeName?; assigneeEmail?; projectId?; projectName?; priority?; estimate?; dueDate?; parentId?; allowZeroEstimate? }>; parallel?; dry_run? }.

HUMAN-READABLE INPUTS (use workspace_metadata to discover valid values):
- priority: 0-4 or "Urgent"/"High"/"Medium"/"Low" (standardized)
- stateType: "completed"/"started"/"backlog"/"unstarted"/"canceled" (standardized)
- stateName/labelNames/assigneeName/projectName: workspace-specific

Behavior: Only send fields you intend to set. If 'assigneeId' is omitted, defaults to current viewer. Invalid numbers are ignored (priority<0 dropped; estimate<=0 dropped unless allowZeroEstimate=true). Returns: per-item results with id/identifier. Next: verify with 'list_issues'.

stateId.description: Workflow state UUID. Or use stateName/stateType for name-based lookup.

stateName.description: State name from your workspace. Use workspace_metadata to see available names.

stateType.description: State type. Finds first matching state. Use when you want "any completed state".

labelNames.description: Label names from your workspace. Use workspace_metadata to see available labels.

assigneeId.description: User UUID. If omitted, defaults to current viewer.

assigneeName.description: User name (fuzzy match). Partial names work. Use workspace_metadata to list users.

assigneeEmail.description: User email to assign (exact match, case-insensitive).

projectName.description: Project name. Resolved to projectId automatically.

allowZeroEstimate.description: If true and estimate=0, sends 0. Otherwise zero is omitted.

dry_run.description: If true, validate but do not create.

tools.name: update_issues
tools.description:
Update issues in batch (state, labels, assignee, metadata). Supports up to 50 items per call — always batch all updates together. Inputs: { items: Array<{ id: string; title?; description?; stateId?; stateName?; stateType?; labelIds?; labelNames?; addLabelIds?; addLabelNames?; removeLabelIds?; removeLabelNames?; assigneeId?; assigneeName?; assigneeEmail?; projectId?; projectName?; priority?; estimate?; dueDate?; parentId?; archived?; allowZeroEstimate? }>; parallel?; dry_run? }.

HUMAN-READABLE INPUTS (use workspace_metadata to discover valid values):
- priority: 0-4 or "Urgent"/"High"/"Medium"/"Low" (standardized)
- stateType: "completed"/"started"/"canceled" (standardized)
- stateName/labelNames/assigneeName/projectName: workspace-specific

Behavior: Only send fields you intend to change. Empty strings ignored; estimate<=0 ignored unless allowZeroEstimate=true. add/removeLabelIds/Names adjust labels incrementally.
Example: { items: [{ id: 'ABC-123', stateType: 'completed', priority: 'High' }] }. Returns: per-item results. Next: 'get_issues' for verification.

id.description: Issue UUID or identifier (e.g. ENG-123). Required.

stateId.description: Workflow state UUID. Or use stateName/stateType for name-based lookup.

stateName.description: State name from issue's team. Use workspace_metadata to see available names.

stateType.description: State type. Finds first matching state.

labelIds.description: Replace all labels with these UUIDs.

labelNames.description: Replace all labels with these names from your workspace.

assigneeName.description: User name (fuzzy match). Partial names work.

assigneeEmail.description: User email to assign (exact match, case-insensitive).

allowZeroEstimate.description: If true and estimate=0, sends 0. Otherwise zero is omitted.

dueDate.description: New due date (YYYY-MM-DD) or empty string to clear.

archived.description: Set true to archive, false to unarchive.

items.description: Issues to update. Batch up to 50.

dry_run.description: If true, validate but do not update.

tools.name: list_teams
tools.description:
List teams in the workspace. Inputs: limit?, cursor?.
Returns: { items: Array<{ id, key?, name }>, cursor?, nextCursor?, limit? }. Next: Use team ids with 'workspace_metadata' (workflowStatesByTeam) and 'list_issues'.

tools.name: list_users
tools.description:
List users in the workspace. Inputs: limit?, cursor?.
Returns: { items: Array<{ id, name?, email?, displayName?, avatarUrl? }>, cursor?, nextCursor?, limit? }. Next: Use user ids in 'update_issues' (assigneeId).

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description:
List comments for an issue. Inputs: { issueId, limit?, cursor? }.
Returns: { items[], cursor?, nextCursor?, limit? } where items include id, body, url?, createdAt, updatedAt?, user{id,name?}. Next: Use add_comments to add context or mention teammates.

tools.name: add_comments
tools.description:
Add one or more comments to issues. Inputs: { items: Array<{ issueId: string; body: string }>, parallel?, dry_run? }.
Returns: per-item results and a summary. Next: Use list_comments to verify and retrieve the comment URLs.

tools.name: update_comments
tools.description:
Update existing comment bodies. Cannot delete comments (by design). Inputs: { items: Array<{ id: string; body: string }> }.
Returns: per-item results and a summary. Next: Use list_comments to verify changes.

tools.name: list_cycles
tools.description:
List cycles for a team (only if team.cyclesEnabled=true). Inputs: { teamId, includeArchived?, orderBy?(updatedAt|createdAt), limit?, cursor? }.
Returns: { items[], cursor?, nextCursor?, limit? } where items include id, name?, number?, startsAt?, endsAt?, completedAt?, teamId, status?. Next: Use teamId from 'workspace_metadata' to target the right team; avoid this tool if cyclesEnabled=false.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description:
List projects with filtering and pagination. Inputs: filter? (ProjectFilter: id/state/team/lead/targetDate), includeArchived?, limit?, cursor?. For a single project, set filter.id.eq and limit=1.
Returns: { items[], cursor?, nextCursor?, limit? } where items include id, name, state, leadId?, teamId?, targetDate?, description?. Next: Use 'update_projects' to modify or 'list_issues' with projectId to find issues.

filter.description: GraphQL-style ProjectFilter. Structure: { field: { comparator: value } }. Examples: { id: { eq: 'PROJECT_UUID' } } for single project, { state: { eq: 'started' } }, { team: { id: { eq: 'TEAM_UUID' } } }, { lead: { id: { eq: 'USER_UUID' } } }, { targetDate: { lt: '2025-01-01', gt: '2024-01-01' } }.

tools.name: create_projects
tools.description:
Create multiple projects in one call. Inputs: { items: Array<{ name: string; teamId?: string; leadId?: string; description?: string; targetDate?: string; state?: string }> }.
Notes: team association uses teamIds internally; provide teamId to attach initially. Returns: per-item results and a summary.

items.description: Projects to create. Use update_projects to change state after creation.

tools.name: update_projects
tools.description:
Update multiple projects in one call. Inputs: { items: Array<{ id: string; name?: string; description?: string; targetDate?: string; state?: string; leadId?: string; archived?: boolean }> }.
Returns: per-item results and a summary. Next: verify with 'list_projects' (filter.id.eq, limit=1); discover via 'list_projects'.

archived.description: Set true to archive, false to unarchive.

tools.name: show_issues_ui
tools.description: Opens an interactive Linear issues dashboard. The UI displays issues in a dark, minimalistic Linear-style interface where users can browse, filter, and manage issues visually. Use this when the user wants to see their issues in a visual interface rather than text output.
